speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Capillary leak syndrome secondary to captopril therapy (captopril-induced vasculopathy).

The patient presents with blisters on the forearm and mucosal ulcers, a classic presentation of drug-induced vasculitis or capillary leak syndrome. Given her recent initiation of captopril, I suspect this is an adverse reaction causing endothelial damage. I will request a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel to check for eosinophilia and renal function, which often accompany this reaction. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

Please confirm if you have noticed any new rashes elsewhere on your body or if the blisters have become purulent.
